question: In 2014 only 3.2% of ammonium values are zero, against 41% in 2013 and 53% in 2015. Were 2014 values not zeroed at the detection limit?
context: Ammonium is left-censored: code 4 = 'value zeroed due to value below detection limit'. The 2014 discontinuity appears in BOTH the bottle table and the CTD-embedded copy, so it is a real feature of that year's reporting rather than a product difference. Any trend fitted through 2014 is distorted. See calcofi.io/workflows/explore_ctd-cast.html

label: Q04
question: 24,579 ammonium values are exactly zero but carry no quality flag, all before 2014. Should the below-detection flag be backfilled?
context: The qual=4 flag is essentially unused before 2013 (0-0.9%) yet exact zeros already run 40-71% in 2008-2012, converging with the flag only after 2015. Filtering on the flag therefore removes ~0% of the early record and ~75% of the late record, manufacturing a trend from a bookkeeping change. Until backfilled, the portable censoring test is measurement_value == 0, not the flag.

label: Q08
question: Some observations in this dataset resolve no CalCOFI grid cell. Are these positions genuinely off-grid (transit, historical stations outside the modern pattern), a coarser spatial notion with no point position, or a coordinate error?
context: 97,985 of 11,135,600 obs rows (0.88%) resolve no CalCOFI grid cell;      0 of those carry no latitude/longitude at all. These are now RELEASED rather than dropped. Are they off-grid positions (transit, historical stations), a coarser spatial notion (region-pooled), or a coordinate error?
proposed_answer: Until v2026.08.10 these rows were DROPPED from `obs` entirely by a `WHERE grid_key IS NOT NULL` filter, while their sampling events stayed in `sample` — so the dataset silently lost them. They are now released with a NULL grid_key. We are not proposing to re-exclude them; we need to know which of the three cases applies so the metadata can say so. A coordinate error is the one that matters most: the sign-flipped Longitude_W on five CalCOFI cruises was invisible precisely because being off-grid removed the rows without a trace.

label: Q09
question: Do the pre-QC R_* columns (R_Oxy_umol/Kg, R_Temp, R_Sal, R_Depth, R_DynHt) share their QC'd counterparts' quality codes (O_qual, T_qual, S_qual, P_qual)?
context: oxygen_umol_kg (Oxy_umol/Kg) carried no quality code in the integrated database until 2026-08-24, so a value with O_qual = 8 (suspect; e.g. cast 19-5508BD-HY-246-2012-07901560, Btl_Cnt 198640, 1144 m, 2.18 ml/L between neighbours at 0.95 and 1.00) plotted as good in every app. It now carries O_qual, as O2ml_L and O2Sat do. The R_* forms still carry none: O_qual code 6 ("data OK but taken from CTD") describes a substitution made DURING QC, so copying it onto the pre-QC value would mislabel ~36k rows. P_qual is read as the pressure/depth code by column position (it sits between S_qual and O_qual, mirroring Depthm/T_degC/Salnty/O2ml_L) while hydro_master_04 reads it as phosphate.
proposed_answer: Leave R_* unflagged (they are the pre-QC record; consumers wanting QC apply the non-R_ type) and treat P_qual as the depth/pressure code (PO4q is the phosphate code). Confirm and we will document both in metadata/measurement_qual.csv.
answer: Confirmed by Rasmus Swalethorp (SIO), 2026-09-01: the pre-QC R_* columns should NOT inherit quality codes from their QC'd counterparts. They are interpolated to standard depths (in decodr), so a flagged depth should already have been skipped by that interpolation; a cast whose T_degC readings are all bad should carry no R_Temp at all. Rasmus: "when we do any kinds of data interpolations ... we should not use already interpolated data points from the bottle database" -- R_* must never be used as an input for further interpolation. metadata/measurement_type.csv now records this as `derivation` on the six r_* types and flips `is_canonical` to FALSE (Q10 of the umbrella 2026-09-03 plan). The other half of this question -- whether P_qual is the pressure/depth code or the phosphate one -- is unresolved and is split out into calcofi_bottle_10 (Q10) for Ben G.
